newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese stocks may rise further 15 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese stocks may rise further 15 pct in 1997.

text.p: Portuguese shares, which have already risen some 54 percent this year, could gain up to 15 percent before the end of 1997, with domestic investors leading the charge, analysts and traders said.
Any slight correction in coming sessions, widely predicted after the recent surge, would be just temporary to let the market catch its breath, analysts said.
"I think the (share) market can rise 10-15 percent before the end of the year," said Joaquim Reis of Central de Investimentos.

Analysts said the market was being driven by an influx of liquidity from small investors who were switching out of fixed term deposits and into investment funds in search of a better return as interest rates hit historic lows.
They said that some funds were receiving inflows of around five billion escudos a day.
"Most six-month fixed deposits (January-June) were not rolled over and it is this money that is being channelled into shares," said Reis.

Analysts noted that fixed-term deposits were yielding no more than a net 3.5 percent and could not compare with the potential gains on a stock market which has been Europe's third best performer this year after Turkey and Greece.
The Portuguese market also gained over 30 percent in 1996.

"Even if the shares of EDP do not rise any further, the simple payment of the dividend will always be more than earnings from term deposits. It is worth investing in shares," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
The state-controlled utility group was partially privatised last month at 2,250 escudos. On Tuesday it stood at 3,330 escudos, down three on the previous close.
"People earned a lot of money in just a few days with EDP and began to believe that in the share market," said Reis.
Analysts expected the market to register a slight correction soon but saw no chance of a crash despite the price surge seen so far this year.

"Even if there is a correction abroad, that will just mean that we will see the foreigners leaving the market, but the domestic investors are not going to let the market fall far," said Jose Freire of Espirito Santo Research.
"Some stocks have already risen above the clouds and are on the way to Mars," he added.

Freire said that the strong rise in Portugal Telecom on Monday, which was being maintained on Tuesday, was explained by the strength of the dollar and by the surge of comparable international shares such as Spain's Telefonica.
Some analysts said that the recent rush into banks, which underperformed in 1996, may have been overdone and this sector could be the first to feel the impact of any profit-taking.
Banco Portugues de Investimento has soared over 100 percent since the start of the year, while other banks have registered gains of over 70 percent.
"After the first half results of the banks, which are expected to be very good, we will be able to distinguish the wheat from the chaff," said Jose Freire.
